messages:
sara_support: FYI customer acme reporting mass embed rejects after a schema migration. They kicked a big backfill and getting lots of 422s - 'vector dimension mismatch: expected 512 got 384'. Also saw a billing spike from retries. Logs attached.
acme_cust: yep — we started a backfill at ~16:40 UTC and by 16:48 started hitting rejects. sample error: \"indexer: insert failed, vector dimension mismatch (expected 512, received 384)\". We're paused now.
james_infra: on it — can you paste the model id used for embedding requests and the backfill batch settings?
sara_support: Model alias: acme-default-embed -> reported model id in requests is \"open-embed-ada-001-v2\" (customer config). Backfill used batch_size=256, concurrency 8.
eli_ml: quick note: open-embed-ada-* variants are 384-dim family in recent lightweight swap; open-embed-512 variants are a different model. Possible alias resolved to a 384 model after today's rollout.
mona_indexer: indexer metrics: rejects spiked to ~1200/min, backlog grew 28k items, retries flooding pipeline. Some tombstones left because backfill timed out mid-batch.
kevin_billing: billing saw a 3x embedding unit spike due to retries. Recommend pausing the backfill to avoid further charges. @ops-bot can you cancel the job id acme-backfill-2026?
ops-bot: cancel-job acme-backfill-2026: queued -> cancelled 
acme_cust: cancelled, thanks. We also saw intermittent 401 errors during the same window — could be unrelated but difficult while debugging.
sara_support: 401s correlate with a short key rotation window at 16:45 UTC in our logs. Seems separate but compounded the outage.
james_infra: I inspected routing configs — alias `acme-default-embed` in region us-east-1 was accidentally pointed to `open-embed-384-lite` as a canary (weight 100) during a rollout. Config snippet from deploy:
```\nroutes:\n  acme-default-embed:\n    - model: open-embed-384-lite\n      region: us-east-1\n      weight: 100\n``` 
eli_ml: recommended options: 1) rollback alias to open-embed-512 (if that's what customer expects), 2) run a full re-embed backfill with the correct model, or 3) create a temporary v384 index to accept 384-dim vectors while they reingest. Padding or truncating vectors is invalid.
mona_indexer: short-term mitigation: I can create a separate table `acme_embeddings_v384` and route 384-dim inserts there so we don't reject and don't overload the main index. Then we can do a controlled reindex later. For safety restart backfill with batch_size=32 and throttle to 50 qps.
sara_support: plan proposal: 1) keep backfill cancelled 2) rollback alias to 512 3) create v384 table and, if customer wants, restart a controlled backfill into v384 4) schedule reindex to unify into v512 later. Also put billing quota hold. Thoughts? :thumbsup:
kevin_billing: I'll put an interim quota and open a credit review for retries.
acme_cust: that's acceptable. Before we restart can you provide a small repro and smoke test we can run?
eli_ml: smoke repro: request 10 docs using the alias and assert embedding length == 512. Example curl: 
```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \\n -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \\n -d '{\"model\":\"acme-default-embed\",\"input\":[\"a\",\"b\"]}'\n``` 
Then check `data[0].embedding | length` in the JSON — should be 512. If it's 384, alias still points to the lite model.
james_infra: I'll rollback the alias now and report back.
ops-bot: alias-update acme-default-embed -> open-embed-512: success
james_infra: rolled back, verified via smoke: embeddings length = 512 for sample requests.
mona_indexer: created `acme_embeddings_v384`, restarted backfill with batch_size=32 and throttle=50 qps. Monitoring rejects now.
sara_support: Customer notified. Also opened an internal postmortem ticket to review rollout gating and alias checks.
acme_cust: backfill progressing, small number of errors but most inserts succeeding. Thanks for quick response.
kevin_billing: billing hold active; I'll follow up with credit proposal after we finish digesting logs.
sara_support: follow-up: scheduling incident review Fri 10:00 UTC. Please include @eng-runtime and @eng-ml. Closing thread once we verify reindex plan.
